items.activity: Write a short phone greeting and a message-taking script for a dental office, then practice it out loud.
items.why: Answering phones is required, and your profile shows greeting people in person but not on the phone.
items.doneWhen: You can greet the caller, take a name, number, and reason for the call, and read it back.
items.evidenceToAdd: Describe what you practiced, as a practice project.
searchSuggestions: how to take a phone message

items.activity: Make a 5-row sample phone message log with time, caller, reason, callback number, and follow-up.
items.why: A small work sample shows you can keep phone messages organized.
items.doneWhen: Every row has all five fields filled in.
items.evidenceToAdd: Add it as a clearly labeled practice project.

items.activity: Ask whether front-desk experience from a restaurant and a school office counts, since the posting says they train you on their scheduling software.
items.why: Dental experience is preferred, not required, and the employer already offers training.
items.doneWhen: You know whether your front-desk experience is accepted.

items.activity: Read an overview of a dental front desk's daily tasks: check-in, insurance cards, scheduling, and payments.
items.why: Knowing the daily routine helps you answer interview questions with confidence.
items.doneWhen: You can describe a typical patient visit from check-in to payment.
